sections.title: ffERG: The ISCEV Standard
content: Dark-Adapted (Scotopic): Measures rod-mediated responses (0.01 and 3.0 ERG).
Light-Adapted (Photopic): Measures cone-mediated responses (3.0 and 30Hz flicker).
a-wave: Hyperpolarization of photoreceptors.
b-wave: Depolarization of ON-bipolar cells.
Oscillatory Potentials: Inner retinal/amacrine cell activity.

sections.title: PERG: Ganglion Cell Integrity
content: P50: Reflects macular/ganglion cell function.
N95: Highly specific marker for ganglion cell dysfunction (e.g., glaucoma, optic neuropathy).
Does not require diffuse retinal health, but requires stable fixation.
Amplitude correlates with the number of functioning RGCs.

sections.title: mfERG: Localized Macular Mapping
content: Produces a 3D topographic map of cone-driven activity in the central 40-50 degrees.
Crucial for diagnosing hydroxychloroquine toxicity (pre-perimetric phase).
Useful in occult macular dystrophies, cone-rod dystrophies, and toxic maculopathies.
N1 (negative deflection) and P1 (positive peak) represent retinal response.

sections.title: Red Flags for Testing
content: Stable fixation is MANDATORY for PERG and mfERG; inaccurate results in nystagmus or poor visual acuity.
Severe media opacities (dense cataract/vitreous hemorrhage) attenuate ffERG results significantly.
Corneal scarring or surface disease alters electrode impedance.
Uncalibrated monitors or non-ISCEV standard protocols lead to misdiagnosis.

sections.title: Diagnostic Workup Process
content: Step 1: Patient dark adaptation (20 mins for scotopic ffERG).
Step 2: Electrode placement (DTL fiber or Gold cup) with thorough corneal anesthesia.
Step 3: Impedance check (ensure low resistance <5kΩ).
Step 4: Stimulus delivery (ISCEV standardized intensity).
Step 5: Waveform analysis comparing patient trace to age-matched laboratory normative data.

content.explanation: P (Photoreceptors = a-wave), B (Bipolar cells = b-wave), O (Others/Amacrine = Oscillatory Potentials).

sections.title: Recent Advances
content: OCT-Angiography correlation with PERG: Mapping microvascular changes in glaucoma.
Artificial Intelligence in automated waveform recognition to reduce human interpretation bias.
Portable handheld ERG devices are improving utility in pediatric and non-clinic environments.
Studies confirm mfERG is superior to standard visual fields for detecting early toxicity.
